transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Hernandez, it's good to see you and your daughter again. I wanted to follow up on the questions you had last time about the developmental screening for your grandson.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hola Doctor. Mi hija me dijo que usted tenía respuestas.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, so I spent some time reviewing the electronic health record. To be completely honest, the error happened because I marked the referral as completed in the system after you declined that first appointment. I didn't set a reminder to follow up, and the system just closed the task. It was my mistake for not ensuring a second attempt was made.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Pero nosotros queríamos ir. Solo que el primer día no pudimos.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. And I am truly sorry for this. I take full responsibility for the fact that we missed the window to get him screened. It is my job to make sure these things happen, and I failed to do that here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just worry if he is behind. He is not talking like the other kids.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you feel anxious about his progress.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. And I thought the clinic was taking care of it. We trusted you. When we didn't hear back, I thought maybe it was just the way things work here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that you feel let down because you trusted us to manage this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like my grandson is losing time. Every month matters at this age. I just don't know if—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, I really have to move quickly because I have a full clinic today, but let's look at the fix. Since the referral was closed, we need to restart the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? Do we start from the beginning?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sort of. I have already placed a priority request with the early intervention team. They should call you by this Friday to schedule a new date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday. And if they don't call?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If you don't have a call by Friday afternoon, I want you to call my nurse, Sarah, directly at the office number. Tell her this is for the priority developmental screen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that. But will the wait be long again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've flagged this as an urgent follow-up due to the previous error, so you should be seen much faster than the first time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope so. I just keep thinking about how much time passed. I feel so sad that we—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go in a few minutes to see my next patient, so let's wrap up. The plan is the phone call by Friday, and then you call Sarah if it doesn't happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, will this happen again? How do I know the computer won't just close it again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I’ve put a manual alert on his chart now. I'll be personally checking the status every Tuesday until I see the final report.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay. I just want him to be okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He will get the help he needs. We'll make sure of it this time. I'll see you at the next check-up.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I really have to move quickly because I have a full clinic today', 'I have to go in a few minutes... let's wrap up').

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the first turn, but there were no comprehension checks (e.g., 'Does that make sense?') throughout the transcript.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am truly sorry'), takes full responsibility ('It was my mistake', 'I failed'), and maintains this under pushback.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions twice ('feel anxious', 'feel let down') and references the patient's shared content regarding trust and the grandson's progress.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (priority request), timelines (by Friday), a named patient role (call Sarah), and prevention (manual alert and Tuesday checks).
